chunks: From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who makes fasting obligatory upon himself in a vow, but he is not strong enough (to fast), he said: He should give to the one who fasts on his behalf, for each day, two mudds.

key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: Two mudds (a unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a person who cannot fast due to weakness after making a vow?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a vow to fast is binding even if the vow-maker lacks the physical strength to fulfill it, requiring compensation through feeding the poor rather than simply breaking the vow. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a *nadr* (vow) creates an obligatory debt, with the specific compensation of two mudds per day serving as a fiduciary substitute for the missed days of worship. This mechanism ensures the spiritual integrity of the vow is maintained through tangible charity, reflecting the practical application of *kaffarah* in personal vows.
